【第1回ペット召喚開催！】
9月28日（月）、9月30日（水）開催。
19時～22時に開催します。
22時以降は主催が起きていればオフ会にします。
最長24時までです。
（この時間に投稿してください、という意味です）

今回のテーマは「自分のペットを自慢しよう！」

あなたはキャラクターのイラストを1枚添付するだけです。
あとはChatGPTがその子の雰囲気や個性を読み取り、「この子に相応しい相棒」を自動で選びます。
そして、その相棒と一緒に新しい1枚のイラストを生成します。
何が選ばれるかは、生成するまでのお楽しみ。
更に、選ばれた相棒の名前もイラスト内に表示されます。

※参加条件を下記に掲載します。

・ChatGPT専用プロンプトなので他のツールで生成しないでください。
・プロンプト使用の際にはフォローしてください。通知が来ないため参加が分からないのでご協力ください。
・自由に使って構いませんが、これはX専用の話です。
・生成イラストを他のサイトへの掲載はお断りします。
・他のツールや商業利用に関するプロンプトの無断開示は禁止されています。
・コラボフリーは相互が前提です。依頼だけして自分からは描かないという方は参加をご遠慮ください。
・プロンプトは下部に記載されています。
・キャラクターの「名前」も含めてください。
・センシ判定の方お断り（私はPCなので見れません）
・ハッシュタグは以下の通り
#ペット召喚 #プロンプト試着
（2つ必須です）
・追加のハッシュタグはお任せです。

コメントの遅れがあったらご容赦ください。

Character Companion Animal Manifestation
— Automatic Companion Selection + Animal Identification —
You are an expert character analyst, animal behavior expert, companion animal designer, and professional anime illustration prompt engineer.
Use the attached character illustration as the only required input.
Do NOT ask the user for the character's name, personality, age, setting, favorite animal, or any additional information.
Your task is to analyze the attached character and independently create one complete illustration in which the character is naturally accompanied by exactly one animal selected specifically for that character.
The selected animal must also be clearly identified with a tasteful, readable information label within the finished illustration.
1. ANALYZE THE CHARACTER
Carefully examine the reference illustration.
Infer, as appropriate:
apparent age and age impression
gender presentation
facial expression
hairstyle and hair color
eye color
clothing and fashion style
dominant colors
accessories
body language
apparent personality
emotional atmosphere
elegance, cuteness, strength, gentleness, intelligence, mystery, playfulness, etc.
implied setting or world
fantasy, modern, historical, futuristic, magical, or other visual themes
overall character identity and aesthetic
Do not invent unnecessary details that contradict the reference image.
The original character must remain clearly recognizable.
2. AUTONOMOUSLY SELECT THE COMPANION ANIMAL
Do not ask the user to choose an animal.
Independently determine which single animal has the strongest overall compatibility with the character.
Consider:
visual harmony
color harmony
apparent personality
emotional compatibility
character's clothing and aesthetic
implied world or setting
size and physical compatibility
natural relationship between character and animal
originality and variety
overall visual appeal
The selected animal should feel as though it genuinely belongs beside this particular character.
Do not simply choose the most common animal.
Avoid repeatedly selecting dogs or cats when another animal would be a stronger match.
3. ANIMAL SELECTION RANGE
The companion may be selected from a very broad range.
Possible choices include, but are not limited to:
dogs
cats
rabbits
hamsters
guinea pigs
ferrets
birds
parrots
owls
songbirds
reptiles
turtles
lizards
snakes
amphibians
fish
horses
ponies
cows
calves
pigs
piglets
sheep
goats
deer
foxes
wolves
bears
raccoons
otters
red pandas
penguins
seals
dolphins
other marine animals
unusual real-world animals
wild animals
domesticated animals
livestock
prehistoric animals
dinosaurs
extinct animals
mythical creatures
fantasy animals
magical beasts
This is NOT a mandatory list.
Choose whatever animal is genuinely the strongest match.
An unusual choice is encouraged when it creates a convincing and aesthetically appealing pairing.
Do not choose an unusual animal merely for novelty.
4. DETERMINE THE EXACT ANIMAL IDENTITY
After selecting the companion, determine its most accurate recognizable identity.
For example:
Golden Retriever
Siberian Husky
Maine Coon
White Rabbit
Red Fox
Arctic Wolf
Emperor Penguin
Highland Cow
Miniature Pig
Barn Owl
Blue Macaw
Velociraptor
Triceratops
When appropriate, identify both:
Common name + specific breed/species
For example:
DOG — SIBERIAN HUSKY
or
WOLF — ARCTIC WOLF
or
CAT — MAINE COON
For prehistoric animals and dinosaurs, use the scientifically recognized common name whenever possible.
For fantasy creatures, use a clear descriptive name such as:
FANTASY CREATURE — ICE DRAGON
The animal identification must correspond exactly to the animal actually depicted.
5. ANIMAL INFORMATION LABEL
The finished illustration MUST contain a small, elegant information panel identifying the selected companion.
Place the information panel in an unobtrusive area such as:
lower corner
lower margin
side margin
elegant translucent panel
small decorative caption area
The information panel must NOT cover the character or animal.
Use a clean, sophisticated typography style that matches the illustration.
The information panel should contain:
COMPANION
[ANIMAL TYPE]
[SPECIES / BREED]
Example:
COMPANION
WOLF
ARCTIC WOLF
Another example:
COMPANION
DOG
SIBERIAN HUSKY
Another example:
COMPANION
DINOSAUR
VELOCIRAPTOR
If the animal has no meaningful breed distinction, simply use:
COMPANION
FOX
RED FOX
The text must be short, clean, correctly spelled, and highly legible.
Do NOT display multiple possible animal names.
Do NOT display the names of animals that were not selected.
6. IMPORTANT TEXT ACCURACY RULE
The animal name displayed in the information panel must match the animal actually generated.
Do not write "CAT" if the image depicts a fox.
Do not write "WOLF" if the image depicts a husky.
Do not write a generic animal name when a clearly identifiable species or breed has been selected.
Prioritize accurate and readable text.
The information panel is part of the composition and should look intentionally designed rather than like an AI-generated random caption.
7. DETERMINE THE RELATIONSHIP
Automatically determine the most natural relationship between the character and the selected animal.
Possible relationships include:
beloved pet
faithful companion
best friend
trusted partner
guardian animal
familiar
magical companion
travel companion
gentle livestock companion
playful friend
protective companion
mysterious companion
majestic partner
Do not explain the relationship in text.
Express it visually through body language and interaction.
8. DESIGN THE ANIMAL
Once the animal has been selected, automatically determine:
species
breed or subtype when appropriate
age
size
fur, feather, scale, or skin characteristics
colors
markings
eye color
facial expression
accessories if appropriate
posture
personality expression
The animal should complement the character without visually overpowering them.
Do not turn an ordinary animal into a fantasy creature unless the character's setting strongly suggests it.
Likewise, do not make the animal excessively cute if that contradicts the character's atmosphere.
9. CHARACTER + ANIMAL COMPOSITION
Place the character and animal together in the same scene.
The animal must be clearly visible.
Possible interactions include:
standing beside the character
sitting beside the character
walking alongside the character
looking up at the character
resting against the character
being gently petted
holding or carrying a small animal when physically appropriate
the character gently touching the animal
the animal affectionately leaning against the character
both looking toward the same direction
playful interaction
protective positioning
elegant side-by-side composition
Choose the most natural interaction automatically.
Avoid awkward poses, unnatural anatomy, forced contact, or physically impossible positioning.
The character remains the primary visual subject.
The animal is the character's companion, not the main subject.
10. PRESERVE THE REFERENCE CHARACTER
The attached image is the primary character reference.
Preserve the character's recognizable identity.
Maintain as accurately as possible:
hairstyle
hair color
eye color
facial characteristics
clothing design
important accessories
distinctive markings
overall appearance
visual identity
Do not unnecessarily redesign the character.
Do not replace the character's outfit unless the reference itself clearly requires adaptation to the new scene.
11. ENVIRONMENT
Automatically create a simple environment that harmonizes with both the character and the selected animal.
The environment may be:
garden
forest
meadow
home
elegant room
city
beach
countryside
fantasy landscape
magical environment
ancient environment
futuristic environment
another suitable location
Choose the environment based on the character and animal.
Do not let the background overpower the subjects.
12. VISUAL QUALITY
Create a polished, high-quality anime illustration.
masterpiece, best quality, ultra detailed, highly detailed anime illustration, beautiful composition, expressive character, detailed animal, natural interaction, coherent lighting, detailed eyes, detailed hair, detailed clothing, detailed animal anatomy, professional character illustration
Use cinematic composition and appealing lighting appropriate to the character.
The character and animal must look like they belong in the same scene.
13. AUTONOMOUS DECISION RULE
The user has intentionally provided only one reference image.
Therefore:
DO NOT ask questions.
DO NOT request a personality description.
DO NOT request the animal type.
DO NOT request the setting.
DO NOT request the relationship.
DO NOT provide multiple animal choices.
Make all necessary creative decisions yourself.
The final output must contain:
1 character
+ exactly 1 selected companion animal
+ 1 clearly readable animal identification panel
FINAL GENERATION DIRECTIVE
Analyze the attached reference image first.
Independently determine the character's visual identity, personality impression, atmosphere, and implied world.
Select exactly one animal that best complements the character.
Determine the exact species or breed of that animal.
Create a finished illustration showing the character and animal naturally together.
Add a small, elegant, highly readable COMPANION information panel identifying the selected animal.
The displayed animal name must accurately match the animal shown.
Do not reveal the analysis process.
Do not present alternatives.
Do not ask questions.
Generate the final illustration directly.

My top 10 Tech Business News for Sept. 20–26, 2026 week.

1. Anthropic launches Claude Opus 5.5
The company says it performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work while costing 40% less to run than Opus 5. API pricing is $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens. 
#Anthropic #Claude #AIModels #AIEconomics

2. Alibaba unveils Zhenwu V900 and a 20 GW AI plan
@AlibabaGroup unveiled its Zhenwu V900 accelerator, which it says delivers three times the performance of its predecessor. It plans mass production in early 2027 and wants Alibaba Cloud’s data-center capacity to exceed 20 gigawatts by 2032. 

My take: Alibaba is pursuing full-stack AI economics: models, chips, cloud and physical capacity. 
#Alibaba #AIChips #DataCenters #ChinaAI

3. @SoftBank launches an $11 billion bond sale for @OpenAI
SoftBank launched $10 billion of dollar-denominated bonds and €1 billion—approximately $1.15 billion—of euro-denominated senior unsecured notes. The financing will support its OpenAI investment and replace a bridge-loan facility. 

My take: As I said repeatedly over last 6-9 months, frontier-model economics is moving into public credit markets. Rising rates are not helping either! 
#SoftBank #OpenAI #AIFinancing #CapitalMarkets

4. AMD crosses a $1 trillion market valuation
@AMD surpassed $1 trillion in market capitalization for the first time on September 21. It became the fourth U.S. chipmaker to reach the milestone, following Nvidia, Broadcom and Micron, as investors continued pricing in AI-driven accelerator and server demand. 

My take: The market is pricing in a multi-vendor accelerator ecosystem, and that's a good thing. 
#AMD #Semiconductors #AIInfrastructure #Markets

5. @SnorkelAI raises $350 million at a $3.5 billion valuation
Snorkel AI raised $350 million as demand increased for specialized training datasets and reinforcement-learning environments. The company's annualized revenue run rate has crossed $350 million, compared with approximately $20 million a year earlier.

My take: Value is migrating outside the base model toward data, evaluations, environments and domain expertise. 
#SnorkelAI #TrainingData #EnterpriseAI #PractitionerEconomics

6. @Apple targets local AI with high-end Macs
Apple is positioning its latest Mac desktops as an alternative to continuously renting centralized AI compute. The company demonstrated four connected Mac Studios running a trillion-parameter model to identify and fix a graphics-code defect. 

My take: Local inference changes AI economics from perpetual token rental toward owned capacity. I still believe that most of the production/runtime inference will be done from Cloud/Datacenters. 
#Apple #LocalAI #EnterpriseComputing #AIEconomics

7. #Accelevation targets up to a $5.4 billion IPO valuation
Data center infrastructure provider Accelevation Holdings is seeking a valuation of up to $5.37 billion in its U.S. IPO. The 

My take: Yet another AI Infra IPO. Investors must distinguish contracted demand from exposure built mainly around the AI narrative.
#Accelevation #IPO #DataCenters #PowerInfrastructure

8. EU orders data-center energy and water disclosures
The European Commission proposed a common rating system requiring data centers with at least 500 kW of capacity to disclose energy and water efficiency. The proposal does not impose consumption limits or require disclosure of total power usage. European data-center capacity is projected to rise from 12 GW in 2025 to 28 GW by 2030. European Commission 

My take: Data-center externalities are becoming operating disclosures. Efficiency scores may influence permits, financing and customer procurement in the long run, turning water and power performance into competitive business metrics.
#EuropeanUnion #DataCenters #EnergyEfficiency #TechPolicy #Regulatiors 

9. AI leaders take the safety debate to the UN
@OpenAI CEO @sma, @AnthropicAI CEO @DarioAmodei and @HuggingFace co-founder Clément Delangue briefed the UN Security Council on September 23 about increasingly capable AI systems and international-security risks. 

My take: AI governance is moving from voluntary laboratory policies into geopolitics. Global agreement may remain dream, so multinational enterprises should expect fragmented safety, deployment and reporting requirements.
#AISafety #UnitedNations #TechPolicy #Governance

10. Fed asks whether AI is becoming “too big to fail”
Kansas City Federal Reserve President Jeff Schmid said regulators need to understand whether the interconnected network of AI companies, contracts and data-center projects is developing into a systemically important ecosystem. 

My take: AI’s systemic risk lies in the network, not one company. Supplier financing, long-duration contracts, leveraged infrastructure and circular customer relationships can transmit a slowdown across model companies, chipmakers, neoclouds, utilities and lenders.
#FederalReserve #AIEconomics #SystemicRisk #DataCenters

==============
AI Model Releases
==============
Qwen-Image-2.1 — Alibaba Qwen
Actual weight release · September 20
A unified image-generation and editing model with a seven-billion-parameter visual-generation component. It supports native transparent-background generation, local editing and as many as 10 reference images. Weights are downloadable, but the Qwen Research License requires separate permission for commercial use. 

Why it matters: Native transparency and multi-reference editing remove production steps, but the restricted license demonstrates that “downloadable weights” does not automatically mean commercially open.

Grok 4.7 — SpaceXAI
Actual proprietary release · September 21
Grok 4.7 uses a larger base model and additional reinforcement learning for coding, agentic tasks and knowledge work. It accepts text and images, has a 500,000-token context window and costs $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens. It is available through the Grok API, Grok Build, Cursor and model gateways. 

Why it matters: Grok 4.7 adds further pricing pressure to frontier coding models. Enterprises should compare cost per completed workflow rather than cost per token alone.

MiMo-V2.6 Pro and Flash — Xiaomi
Actual open-weight release · September 21
MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL is a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 1.02 trillion total parameters and 42 billion activated per token. Flash uses 309 billion total and 15 billion activated parameters. Both provide one-million-token context and native text, image, video and audio inputs. The Hugging Face model pages label the weights MIT-licensed; hosted access is also available through Xiaomi services and OpenRouter. 

Why it matters: Xiaomi is combining large open weights, omnimodal inputs and long context with public deployment recipes. That increases the ability of enterprises and sovereign AI programs to operate capable models on infrastructure they control.

Claude Opus 5.5 — Anthropic
Actual proprietary release · September 22
The text-and-vision model supports one million context tokens and up to 128,000 output tokens. Anthropic reports lower serving costs, faster output and stronger safeguards than Opus 5. It is available through Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry. 

Why it matters: Anthropic is moving capability previously reserved for premium models into a lower-cost operating envelope, increasing pressure on both closed and open-weight competitors.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna — OpenAI
Actual proprietary release · September 22
Sol targets complex coding and agentic workflows, while Luna targets focused, high-volume workloads. Both accept text and images, offer 1.05-million-token context windows and are available through the API, ChatGPT Work and Codex. Standard API pricing is $2/$10 per million input/output tokens for Sol and $0.10/$0.50 for Luna. OpenAI API changelog | Model catalog OpenAI API

Why it matters: OpenAI is explicitly segmenting intelligence by workload economics. Luna’s pricing makes model routing and high-volume agent orchestration substantially more attractive.

FLUX 3 Action — Black Forest Labs
Actual open-weight release · September 23
FLUX 3 Action is a seven-billion-parameter world-action model for robotics and other embodied tasks. It jointly predicts future frames and actions from camera observations, system state and text instructions. Weights use the FLUX Kommunity License v1.0, while the training code and fine-tuning recipes are public. Black Forest Labs https://t.co/VZGbQz3www

Why it matters: Physical AI is moving beyond vision-language understanding toward models that predict and execute actions. This expands model economics into robots, edge hardware and industrial systems.

Alibaba’s five-to-10-trillion-parameter model
Development plan announced September 22—not a release. Alibaba disclosed plans for a model up to four times larger than Qwen 3.8 Max. No completed model, weights, API, license or release date was announced. It should therefore be treated as a roadmap statement rather than an available model. 

My Work: It was a busy travel week. included 4 days Toronto visit, returning home and attending the #WeAreDevelopers conference in San Jose on Friday. At @WeAreDevelopers, I spoke to @Docker (on camera), @JPMorgan (on camera), @IBM, @AWScloud, and @GoogleCloud folks. My most notable talk (on camera) was with WeAreDevelopers organizers. Will post video this week. 

OpenAI–Anthropic agreement to stress-test each other’s models—closely aligning with this week’s broader safety and governance theme. 

My question to you: Which layer do you think will produce the most durable AI returns: models, chips, specialized data, local compute or infrastructure financing?
